stem.en: Family planning programmes were initiated in India in:

explanation.en: India was among the first countries to start family planning at the national level, in 1951.

stem.en: Amniocentesis is a test that studies:

options.en: the sperm count of the father
the chromosomal pattern of foetal cells in the amniotic fluid
the blood group of the mother

explanation.en: Cells from the amniotic fluid are examined for chromosomal disorders.

stem.en: The statutory ban on amniocentesis for sex determination aims to:

explanation.en: The test was misused to abort female foetuses, so it is banned for sex determination.

stem.en: RCH stands for:

explanation.en: The improved family-planning programmes are called Reproductive and Child Health Care (RCH) programmes.

stem.en: In periodic abstinence, couples avoid coitus from:

options.en: day 10 to day 17 of the cycle
day 1 to day 5 of the cycle
day 20 to day 28 of the cycle

explanation.en: Ovulation is expected around the middle of the cycle, so days 10–17 are treated as the fertile period.

stem.en: Lactational amenorrhea is effective only up to about:

explanation.en: Ovulation usually does not occur during intense breastfeeding, up to about six months after birth.

stem.en: Which contraceptive also protects against sexually transmitted infections?

explanation.en: Condoms are a physical barrier and so also reduce the risk of STIs and AIDS.

stem.en: The legal marriageable age in India is:

options.en: 21 years for females and 18 years for males
18 years for females and 21 years for males
16 years for females and 18 years for males

explanation.en: Raising the marriageable age is one of the measures for population control.

stem.en: Which of these is a hormone-releasing IUD?

explanation.en: Progestasert and LNG-20 release hormones; CuT, Cu7 and Multiload 375 release copper.

stem.en: Saheli, an oral contraceptive pill, is:

options.en: non-steroidal and taken once a week

explanation.en: Saheli was developed at CDRI, Lucknow; it is a non-steroidal once-a-week pill.

stem.en: In vasectomy, the part cut and tied is the:

explanation.en: Vasectomy blocks the vas deferens; tubectomy blocks the fallopian tube.

stem.en: Copper ions released by CuT prevent pregnancy mainly by:

options.en: suppressing sperm motility and fertilising capacity
killing the ovum in the ovary

explanation.en: Cu ions reduce sperm motility and fertilising ability; IUDs also increase phagocytosis of sperm.

solution.en: Cu ions reduce sperm motility and fertilising ability; IUDs also increase phagocytosis of sperm.

stem.en: Emergency contraceptives are effective if used within:

explanation.en: Progestogens, alone or with estrogens, given within 72 hours of unprotected coitus can prevent pregnancy.

stem.en: MTP was legalised in India in the year:

explanation.en: India legalised medical termination of pregnancy in 1971; the Act was amended in 2017.

stem.en: MTP is considered relatively safe during the:

explanation.en: MTPs are relatively safe up to 12 weeks of pregnancy.

stem.en: Which STI is NOT completely curable?

explanation.en: Hepatitis B, genital herpes and HIV infections are not completely curable.

stem.en: Which of these is NOT transmitted sexually?

explanation.en: Typhoid spreads through contaminated food and water; the others are STIs.

solution.en: Typhoid spreads through contaminated food and water; the others are STIs.

stem.en: According to the MTP (Amendment) Act, 2017, a pregnancy between 12 and 24 weeks can be terminated on the opinion of:

explanation.en: Up to 12 weeks needs one RMP; 12–24 weeks needs two RMPs, on specified grounds.

stem.en: In ZIFT, the zygote or early embryo is transferred into the:

explanation.en: ZIFT: zygote intra-fallopian transfer of embryos with up to 8 blastomeres.

stem.en: ICSI is a technique in which:

options.en: an embryo is transferred into the uterus
an ovum is transferred into the fallopian tube
semen is placed in the uterus
a sperm is injected directly into the ovum

explanation.en: Intra-cytoplasmic sperm injection forms an embryo in the laboratory.

stem.en: Artificial insemination is used mainly when:

options.en: the embryo has more than 8 blastomeres
the male has a very low sperm count

explanation.en: AI introduces semen from the husband or a donor into the vagina or uterus (IUI).

stem.en: An embryo with more than 8 blastomeres is transferred into the uterus by:

explanation.en: IUT is intra-uterine transfer; ZIFT is for embryos up to 8 blastomeres.

solution.en: IUT is intra-uterine transfer; ZIFT is for embryos up to 8 blastomeres.

stem.en: GIFT is suitable for a woman who:

options.en: cannot carry a pregnancy in the uterus
cannot produce ova but can provide a suitable environment for fertilisation
has a partner with low sperm count only

explanation.en: In GIFT a donor ovum is placed in her fallopian tube, so her tubes must be functional.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): Copper-releasing IUDs such as CuT are effective contraceptives.
Reason (R): Copper ions released by the device suppress sperm motility and the fertilising capacity of sperms.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: NCERT: Cu ions released suppress sperm motility and fertilising capacity, which is why CuT and Cu7 work.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): Vasectomy is a terminal (permanent) method of contraception in males.
Reason (R): In vasectomy, a small part of the fallopian tube is removed or tied up.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: Vasectomy removes or ties a small part of the vas deferens through a small incision on the scrotum; removing part of the fallopian tube is tubectomy, done in females.

passage.en: A couple has been unable to have a child for four years. Tests show that the husband's semen has a normal sperm count and motility. The wife's ovaries release normal ova, but both her fallopian tubes are blocked. The doctor suggests collecting ova from the wife and sperm from the husband and fusing them in the laboratory.

stem.en: Which technique is most suitable for this couple?

options.en: Intra-uterine insemination (IUI) of the husband's semen
In vitro fertilisation followed by embryo transfer

explanation.en: Blocked tubes stop the sperm and ovum from meeting inside the body, so IUI and GIFT (which needs a functional tube) will fail; IVF-ET bypasses the tubes. Donor semen is not needed as the husband's semen is normal.

passage.en: A couple has been unable to have a child for four years. Tests show that the husband's semen has a normal sperm count and motility. The wife's ovaries release normal ova, but both her fallopian tubes are blocked. The doctor suggests collecting ova from the wife and sperm from the husband and fusing them in the laboratory.

stem.en: The embryo formed in the laboratory reaches the 16-blastomere stage. Where should it be placed, and by which technique?

explanation.en: Embryos with more than 8 blastomeres are transferred into the uterus (intra-uterine transfer); ZIFT is for zygotes or embryos up to 8 blastomeres, and her tubes are blocked anyway.

stem.en: Match Column I with Column II. Column I: (a) Lippes loop (b) Multiload 375 (c) LNG-20 (d) Saheli. Column II: (i) hormone-releasing IUD (ii) non-medicated IUD (iii) once-a-week oral pill (iv) copper-releasing IUD.

explanation.en: Lippes loop is non-medicated; Multiload 375 releases copper; LNG-20 releases hormone; Saheli is a once-a-week non-steroidal pill.

solution.en: Lippes loop is non-medicated; Multiload 375 releases copper; LNG-20 releases hormone; Saheli is a once-a-week non-steroidal pill.

stem.en: Which of the following is correctly matched?

options.en: ZIFT: embryo with more than 8 blastomeres transferred into the uterus
IUT: embryo with more than 8 blastomeres transferred into the uterus
GIFT: zygote transferred into the fallopian tube
ICSI: semen introduced into the uterus

explanation.en: IUT transfers an embryo with more than 8 blastomeres into the uterus. ZIFT transfers a zygote or embryo of up to 8 blastomeres into the fallopian tube; GIFT transfers an ovum; ICSI injects a sperm into the ovum.

stem.en: Which group contains only sexually transmitted infections that are completely curable if detected early and treated properly?

explanation.en: Except hepatitis B, genital herpes and HIV, the common STIs are completely curable if detected early. Only the first group avoids all three.

solution.en: Except hepatitis B, genital herpes and HIV, the common STIs are completely curable if detected early.
Only the first group avoids all three.

stem.en: Which statement about natural and barrier methods is incorrect?

options.en: Periodic abstinence avoids coitus from day 10 to day 17 of the cycle
Lactational amenorrhea is effective only up to about six months after parturition
Condoms protect against STIs as well as pregnancy
Diaphragms and cervical caps are single-use and cannot be reused

explanation.en: Diaphragms, cervical caps and vaults are reusable. The other three statements are correct.

stem.en: According to the MTP (Amendment) Act, 2017 as described in NCERT, terminating a pregnancy between 12 and 24 weeks requires

options.en: the opinion of one registered medical practitioner
the opinion of two registered medical practitioners

explanation.en: Up to 12 weeks, one registered medical practitioner's opinion is enough; between 12 and 24 weeks, two registered medical practitioners must give their opinion.

stem.en: According to the World Health Organisation (WHO), reproductive health means:

explanation.en: WHO defines reproductive health as total well-being in all aspects of reproduction, i.e. physical, emotional, behavioural and social. A society with people whose reproductive organs are physically and functionally normal and who interact normally in emotional and behavioural aspects of sex is reproductively healthy. Normal organs alone (option 2) are not enough.

options.en: Only the absence of reproductive diseases
Total well-being in all aspects of reproduction: physical, emotional, behavioural and social
The ability to produce a large number of children

stem.en: India was among the first countries in the world to initiate action plans at the national level for family planning. These were started in:

explanation.en: Family planning programmes were initiated in India in 1951 and were periodically assessed over the past decades. 1971 is the year MTP was legalised in India.

stem.en: Improved family-planning programmes in India, covering wider reproduction-related areas, are popularly called:

explanation.en: Improved programmes covering wider reproduction-related areas are currently in operation under the popular name Reproductive and Child Health Care (RCH) programmes. They create awareness and provide medical assistance and care to build a reproductively healthy society.

options.en: Reproductive and Child Health Care (RCH) programmes

stem.en: A statutory ban on amniocentesis for sex determination was imposed in India to:

explanation.en: Amniocentesis is a foetal sex-determination test based on the chromosomal pattern of cells in the amniotic fluid surrounding the developing embryo. Because it was misused to detect a female foetus and terminate the pregnancy, a statutory ban on its use for sex determination was imposed to legally check increasing female foeticide. It is still used to detect genetic disorders.

options.en: Reduce the cost of antenatal care

stem.en:
Statement I: The world population, which was around 2 billion in 1900, rose to about 6 billion by 2000 and 7.2 billion in 2011.
Statement II: India's population, about 350 million at the time of independence, crossed 1.2 billion in May 2011.

explanation.en: Both are NCERT figures. World: ~2 billion (1900) → ~6 billion (2000) → 7.2 billion (2011). India: ~350 million at independence → close to 1 billion by 2000 → crossed 1.2 billion in May 2011. Such rapid growth comes from a fall in death rate, MMR and IMR and an increase in the number of people of reproducible age.

options.en: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

stem.en: Which of the following is NOT cited as a reason for the population explosion in India?

explanation.en: Population grows when deaths fall while births continue. NCERT lists a rapid decline in death rate, MMR and IMR, and an increase in people of reproducible age. A rise in child death rate would reduce growth, so option 4 is not a reason.

options.en: Decline in maternal mortality rate (MMR) and infant mortality rate (IMR)
Increase in the number of people of reproducible age
A sharp rise in the death rate of children under five

stem.en: Which of the following is NOT a property of an ideal contraceptive?

explanation.en: An ideal contraceptive should be user-friendly, easily available, effective and reversible, with no or least side effects, and should not interfere with sexual drive, desire or the sexual act. Irreversibility and side effects are the opposite of ideal.

options.en: Does not interfere with sexual drive or act

stem.en: In the periodic abstinence method, couples avoid coitus during the days when ovulation can be expected, which are about:

explanation.en: In periodic abstinence, couples avoid coitus from day 10 to 17 of the menstrual cycle, when ovulation could be expected. Chances of fertilisation are very high in this period, so it is called the fertile period. Days 1–5 are the menstrual phase.

stem.en: Lactational amenorrhea as a natural contraceptive method is effective only up to a maximum of:

explanation.en: Lactational amenorrhea is based on the fact that ovulation, and therefore the cycle, does not occur during the period of intense lactation after parturition. As long as the mother breastfeeds the child fully, chances of conception are almost nil, but this works only up to a maximum of six months after parturition.

stem.en: Coitus interruptus is a natural method of contraception in which:

explanation.en: Coitus interruptus (withdrawal) is the method in which the male partner withdraws his penis from the vagina just before ejaculation to avoid insemination. Option 1 is periodic abstinence; options 3 and 4 are barrier methods.

options.en: Coitus is avoided between days 10 and 17
The male partner withdraws his penis from the vagina just before ejaculation
A rubber sheath covers the penis

stem.en: 'Nirodh' is a popular brand of:

explanation.en: Condoms are barriers made of thin rubber or latex sheath used to cover the penis in the male, or the vagina and cervix in the female, just before coitus. 'Nirodh' is a popular brand of condom for the male. Condoms also protect the user from STIs and AIDS.

stem.en: Diaphragms, cervical caps and vaults are:

explanation.en: Diaphragms, cervical caps and vaults are barriers made of rubber, inserted into the female reproductive tract to cover the cervix during coitus. They prevent conception by blocking the entry of sperms through the cervix and are reusable. Spermicidal creams, jellies and foams are usually used with them to increase contraceptive efficiency.

options.en: Single-use hormonal barriers inserted into the uterus
Reusable rubber barriers inserted into the female reproductive tract to cover the cervix during coitus
Intra-uterine devices that release copper ions

stem.en:
Match the intra-uterine device with its type:
A. Lippes loop
B. Multiload 375
C. LNG-20
D. Cu7
I. Copper-releasing IUD
II. Hormone-releasing IUD
III. Non-medicated IUD

explanation.en: NCERT classes IUDs as non-medicated (Lippes loop), copper-releasing (CuT, Cu7, Multiload 375) and hormone-releasing (Progestasert, LNG-20). So A-III, B-I, C-II, D-I. Multiload 375 is copper-releasing; students who don't remember the name often mark it hormonal.

stem.en: Copper ions released from copper-releasing IUDs act by:

explanation.en: IUDs increase phagocytosis of sperms within the uterus, and the Cu ions released suppress sperm motility and the fertilising capacity of sperms. Inhibiting ovulation is the main action of oral pills, not of copper IUDs.

options.en: Suppressing sperm motility and the fertilising capacity of sperms

stem.en:
Assertion (A): Hormone-releasing IUDs are effective contraceptives.
Reason (R): They make the uterus unsuitable for implantation and the cervix hostile to sperms.

explanation.en: NCERT: 'The hormone-releasing IUDs, in addition, make the uterus unsuitable for implantation and the cervix hostile to the sperms.' This is exactly why they work, so R correctly explains A.

options.en: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

stem.en: IUDs are ideal contraceptives for females who:

explanation.en: IUDs are inserted by doctors or expert nurses into the uterus through the vagina, and are ideal for females who want to delay pregnancy and/or space children. They are widely accepted in India. They do not protect against STIs, and they are reversible, unlike sterilisation.

options.en: Want to delay pregnancy and/or space children

stem.en: Oral contraceptive pills are usually taken daily for a period of:

explanation.en: Pills (progestogens alone or progestogen–estrogen combinations) are taken daily for 21 days, starting preferably within the first five days of the menstrual cycle. After a gap of 7 days, during which menstruation occurs, they are taken again in the same pattern until the female wants to stop.

options.en: 21 days, starting preferably within the first five days of the cycle, followed by a 7-day gap
28 days continuously from the day of ovulation
14 days, starting on the day of ovulation

stem.en:
How many of the following are actions of combined (progestogen–estrogen) oral contraceptive pills?
(i) Inhibit ovulation
(ii) Inhibit implantation
(iii) Alter the quality of cervical mucus to prevent or retard entry of sperms
(iv) Increase phagocytosis of sperms within the uterus
(v) Block the fallopian tubes surgically

explanation.en: NCERT: pills inhibit ovulation and implantation and alter the quality of cervical mucus to prevent or retard entry of sperms (i–iii). Increased phagocytosis of sperms (iv) is an action of IUDs, and tubal blocking (v) is tubectomy. So three.

stem.en: 'Saheli', a new oral contraceptive for females, was developed by scientists at:

explanation.en: Saheli was developed by scientists at the Central Drug Research Institute (CDRI) in Lucknow, India. It is a once-a-week pill with very few side effects and high contraceptive value.

stem.en:
Statement I: Saheli has very few side effects and high contraceptive value.
Statement II: Saheli is a steroidal preparation that must be taken every day.

explanation.en: Statement I is correct. Statement II is wrong: Saheli is a non-steroidal preparation taken once a week, unlike the daily steroidal pills.

options.en: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

stem.en: Administration of progestogens or progestogen–estrogen combinations, or insertion of an IUD, can be used as an emergency contraceptive if done within:

explanation.en: These methods are very effective as emergency contraceptives when used within 72 hours of coitus, for example after rape or casual unprotected intercourse.

stem.en: In vasectomy:

explanation.en: Sterilisation in the male is vasectomy: a small part of the vas deferens is removed or tied up through a small incision on the scrotum. In the female, tubectomy removes or ties up a small part of the fallopian tube through a small incision in the abdomen or through the vagina.

options.en: A small part of the fallopian tube is removed or tied up
A small part of the vas deferens is removed or tied up through a small incision on the scrotum
A copper device is inserted into the urethra

stem.en:
Assertion (A): Surgical methods of contraception are generally advised only as a terminal method.
Reason (R): Surgical methods block gamete transport and are highly effective, but their reversibility is very poor.

explanation.en: Vasectomy and tubectomy block gamete transport and are highly effective. However, their reversibility is very poor, so they are advised for the male or female partner as a terminal method to prevent any more pregnancies. R explains A.

options.en: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

stem.en: The Government of India legalised medical termination of pregnancy (MTP), with strict conditions to avoid its misuse, in:

explanation.en: The Government of India legalised MTP in 1971 with strict conditions to avoid its misuse, e.g. indiscriminate and illegal female foeticide. 1951 is the year family planning programmes began.

stem.en: Worldwide, approximately how many MTPs are performed every year?

explanation.en: Nearly 45 to 50 million MTPs are performed in a year all over the world, which accounts for about one-fifth of the total number of conceived pregnancies in a year.

stem.en: MTPs are considered relatively safe when performed during:

explanation.en: MTPs are relatively safe during the first trimester, i.e. up to 12 weeks of pregnancy. Second-trimester abortions are much more risky. A dangerous trend is that a majority of MTPs are performed illegally by unqualified quacks, which are unsafe and could be fatal.

stem.en: Under the Indian law on medical termination of pregnancy as described in NCERT, a pregnancy that has lasted more than 12 weeks but fewer than 24 weeks may be terminated on considered grounds only if:

explanation.en: Within the first 12 weeks a pregnancy may be terminated on the opinion of one registered medical practitioner. If it has lasted more than 12 but fewer than 24 weeks, two registered medical practitioners must be of the opinion, formed in good faith, that the required grounds exist. Option 1 is the rule for the first 12 weeks only. (Note: the MTP (Amendment) Act, 2021 now allows termination on one RMP's opinion up to 20 weeks and needs two RMPs for 20–24 weeks in special categories; NCERT and NEET questions use the 12/24-week rule above.)

options.en: One registered medical practitioner gives the opinion
Two registered medical practitioners are of the opinion, formed in good faith, that the required grounds exist
The woman's consent alone is obtained
A court order is obtained in every case

stem.en: Which of the following is NOT a sexually transmitted infection?

explanation.en: Gonorrhoea, syphilis, genital herpes, chlamydiasis, genital warts, trichomoniasis, hepatitis-B and HIV are common STIs. Typhoid spreads through contaminated food and water, not by sexual contact.

stem.en: Except for which group are all the other diseases/infections completely curable if detected early and treated properly?

explanation.en: NCERT: except for hepatitis-B, genital herpes and HIV infections, other STIs are completely curable if detected early and treated properly. The others listed are bacterial, protozoan or treatable infections.

options.en: Hepatitis-B, genital herpes and HIV infection

stem.en: The incidence of STIs is reported to be very high among persons in the age group of:

explanation.en: Though all persons are vulnerable to STIs, their incidence is reported to be very high among persons in the 15–24 years age group, the age group to which many students belong.

stem.en:
How many of the following are listed in NCERT as possible complications of STIs that are not detected and treated in time?
(i) Pelvic inflammatory disease (PID)
(ii) Abortions and still births
(iii) Ectopic pregnancies
(iv) Infertility
(v) Cancer of the reproductive tract
(vi) Down's syndrome in the mother

explanation.en: Untreated STIs can lead to PID, abortions, still births, ectopic pregnancies, infertility or even cancer of the reproductive tract: items (i)–(v). Down's syndrome is a chromosomal (trisomy 21) disorder, not an STI complication. So five.

stem.en:
Match the assisted reproductive technology with its description:
A. ZIFT
B. IUT
C. GIFT
D. ICSI
I. Transfer of an ovum collected from a donor into the fallopian tube of a female who cannot produce ova
II. A sperm is injected directly into the ovum to form an embryo in the laboratory
III. Transfer of the zygote or early embryo (up to 8 blastomeres) into the fallopian tube
IV. Transfer of an embryo with more than 8 blastomeres into the uterus

explanation.en: ZIFT (zygote intra-fallopian transfer): zygote or early embryo up to 8 blastomeres into the fallopian tube (III). IUT (intra-uterine transfer): embryo with more than 8 blastomeres into the uterus (IV). GIFT (gamete intra-fallopian transfer): ovum from a donor into the fallopian tube of a female who cannot produce ova but can provide a suitable environment (I). ICSI: a sperm is directly injected into the ovum (II). Option 1 swaps ZIFT and IUT, the usual confusion.

stem.en: Gamete intra-fallopian transfer (GIFT) is recommended for a female who:

explanation.en: In GIFT, an ovum collected from a donor is transferred into the fallopian tube of another female who cannot produce ova but can provide suitable conditions for fertilisation and further development. Low sperm count is usually managed by artificial insemination or ICSI.

options.en: Produces ova but has blocked fallopian tubes
Has a male partner with a very low sperm count only
Cannot produce ova but can provide suitable conditions for fertilisation and development

stem.en: In artificial insemination (AI), including intra-uterine insemination (IUI), the semen collected from the husband or a healthy donor is:

explanation.en: AI is used where the male partner cannot inseminate the female or has very low sperm counts. Semen from the husband or a healthy donor is artificially introduced into the vagina or into the uterus (IUI). Option 1 is ICSI; option 3 is IVF with embryo transfer.

options.en: Injected directly into the ovum in the laboratory
Artificially introduced into the vagina or into the uterus of the female
Mixed with the ovum in a test tube and the zygote is transferred
Frozen and transferred into the fallopian tube along with the ovum

stem.en:
Assertion (A): In vitro fertilisation followed by embryo transfer is popularly known as the 'test tube baby' programme.
Reason (R): In this method, ova from the wife or a donor and sperms from the husband or a donor are collected and induced to form a zygote under simulated conditions in the laboratory.

explanation.en: IVF means fertilisation outside the body in almost similar conditions as in the body, followed by embryo transfer (ET). Because the zygote is formed in the laboratory ('in a test tube'), the programme is called the test tube baby programme. R describes exactly that, so it explains A.

options.en: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

stem.en:
Statement I: Embryos formed by in vivo fertilisation (fusion of gametes within the female) can also be used for embryo transfer to assist females who cannot conceive.
Statement II: ICSI is the technique used when the female cannot produce ova.

explanation.en: Statement I is an NCERT line: embryos formed by in vivo fertilisation can also be transferred. Statement II is wrong: when the female cannot produce ova, GIFT is used (donor ovum into her fallopian tube). ICSI injects a sperm directly into an ovum and is used mainly for male infertility.

options.en: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
